1: # pathland-render-qt — implementation status
2: 
3: **Last updated:** September 24, 2026
4: 
5: The **Qt Quick renderer**: maps opcode frames incrementally onto a Qt Quick
6: scene graph (shared-memory desktop path). Protocol contract: `spec/`.
7: Design-token contract: `spec/TOKENS.md`.
8: 
9: **Language split.** The crate is a **hybrid**:
10: - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), a sent-state
11:   **delta diff** that turns each frame into a batch of C-compatible commands,
12:   the `Pump` transport seam (frames in / events out), the Qt main-loop shell,
13:   and the C ABI for foreign hosts.
14: - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell (QGuiApplication +
15:   QQuickWindow + QQmlEngine + a QML-facing `Bridge` QObject) and applies the
16:   delta command batch to QML items. Built via `cc` + `moc` in `build.rs`;
17:   needs Qt6 dev libs (Homebrew: `qtbase qtdeclarative`).
18: 
19: ## Implemented
20: 
21: - **Build/toolchain**: `build.rs` locates Qt via `qmake -query` (Homebrew +
22:   Linux CI), runs `moc` on the bridge, compiles the C++ layer with `cc`, and
23:   links the Qt frameworks/dylibs (framework search via the transitive
24:   `rustc-link-search=framework` kind, so demo binaries link too). The protocol
25:   core (`pathland-core`/`view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
26: - **FFI boundary** (`src/ffi.rs` + `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`): a flat
27:   `PathlandQtCommand` batch (create/delete/insert/remove/move/set-text/
28:   set-property/set-string-property/reset-node/set-scheme) plus a
29:   `PathlandQtEvent` (pointer-up/value-changed/text-changed) flowing C++ → Rust.
30: - **Delta diff** (`src/renderer.rs`): `QtRenderer` keeps a sent-state cache and
31:   emits only the commands that change it — an unchanged tree emits **zero**
32:   commands. Property changes re-send the node's *complete* property set
33:   preceded by `RESET_NODE` (so the C++ layer resets removed properties to
34:   renderer defaults). Numeric props are emitted with `VALUE` last (Qt Quick
35:   clamps a control's value when `from`/`to` aren't configured yet). Tree roots
36:   are children of pseudo-parent `0` (window contentItem). Ghost children after
37:   `DELETE_NODE` are guarded in the walk. Headless-tested.
38: - **Qt widget mapping** (`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`): component → QML item factory —
39:   `VSTACK`/`HSTACK`/lazy stacks → `Column`/`Row`, `GRID`+lazy grids → `Grid`,
40:   `ZSTACK` → `Item`, `SCROLLVIEW` → `ScrollView`, `TEXT` → `Text`, `SPACER`/
41:   unknown → `Item`, `DIVIDER` → `Rectangle`, `COLOR`/`SHAPE` → `Rectangle`,
42:   `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`
43:   → `Slider`, `TOGGLE` → `Switch` (controls embed `onX: bridge.<event>(id, …)`
44:   handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
45:   activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
46:   (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
47:   `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
48:   (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
49:   `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
50:   native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
51:   (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
52:   FILL → `anchors.fill`, `-2` HUG → implicit), color, font size/weight/family,
53:   opacity, visible, z, value/min/max/step, selected→checked, enabled,
54:   `IS_SECURE` → `echoMode`, progress/indeterminate, selection→currentIndex,
55:   prompt/label→placeholder, image source. `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned
56:   style defaults (value props untouched so a slider/toggle doesn't lose
57:   position on echo).
58: - **Events** (spec/EVENTS.md guards): the `Bridge` reports control inputs
59:   (`tap` → `POINTER_UP`, `valueChanged` → `VALUE_CHANGED`, `textChanged` →
60:   `TEXT_CHANGED`) to Rust, which encodes the `Event`, writes it into the event
61:   ring, and wakes the host (renderer never drains). Interactions are gated by
62:   `BINDING_ID`/`ACTION_ID` and programmatic value sets suppress echoes.
63: - **Pointer event streams**: an `EVENT_LISTENERS`-gated QML `MouseArea` overlay
64:   is attached to any node carrying pointer listener bits (down/move/up), and
65:   its handlers report `POINTER_DOWN`/`POINTER_MOVE`/`POINTER_UP` through the
66:   Bridge (bypassing the `BINDING_ID` gate — any element can emit raw inputs,
67:   spec/EVENTS.md). Attached/detached on listener-mask changes / `RESET` /
68:   `DELETE`.
69: - **Native back / `NAVIGATE`**: a window-level `KeyFilter` maps Escape to
70:   `Event::Navigate { url: None }` (global, never node-keyed), matching the GTK
71:   renderer. BackSpace is deferred (needs text-focus detection).
72: - **Color-scheme detection (spec/TOKENS.md)**: `QStyleHints::colorSchemeChanged`
73:   fires a scheme event to Rust, which calls `QtRenderer::set_scheme` — the
74:   shared core re-resolves design tokens and the diff re-emits the changed
75:   concrete values (`SET_PROPERTY`) with no host wake. Initial scheme applied at
76:   init.
77: - **`META::RESET`**: both pump paths scan each frame for `META::RESET` and call
78:   `QtRenderer::reset()` (clears the decoded tree, sent-state cache, and the
79:   C++ scene incl. listener overlays).
80: - **Qt shell**: init/run split (headless tests drive `init` + `apply` without
81:   an event loop); `pathland_qt_layer_run` owns the window + a zero-millisecond
82:   idle `QTimer` that ticks Rust's pump (Qt analogue of GTK's idle pump).
83: - **C ABI for foreign hosts** (`src/capi.rs`): `pathland_qt_run(host,
84:   on_event)` (over a `pathland-view-native` `NativeHost`) and
85:   `pathland_qt_run_ring(ring, on_event, width, height)` (over a borrowed
86:   `libpathland_core` ring), both mirroring the GTK renderer's contract. Passes
87:   a bare program name to Qt.
88: - **Rust demo ergonomics** (`run`): `pathland_qt::run(app_id, title,
89:   Rc<RefCell<RingTransport>>, on_event)` mirrors `pathland_render_gtk::run`;
90:   the pump borrow is held across frame application (zero-copy batch view of the
91:   shared ring).
92: 
93: - **Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5)**: a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying the
94:   `ROUTE` property promotes to the renderer's nav container and reconciles a
95:   page stack **by depth** (`NAV_DEPTH`): pop down to the app's depth, then
96:   `Refresh` (same route), `Push` (deeper + new route), or `Replace` (same
97:   depth, new route) — mirroring the GTK `AdwNavigationView` adapter. `PlatformDefault`
98:   chrome wraps each page in a header with a native back button (`→`
99:   `navigateBack` → `Event::Navigate { url: None }`); `NAV_CHROME=1` (`Custom`)
100:   pushes the bare destination. The back-stack stays app-owned; the page stack
101:   is the renderer's rendered-output cache. **Implementation note:** Qt Quick
102:   has no native navigation container and `StackView`'s `push`/`pop` are
103:   QML-callable-only (not invokable from C++ via `QMetaObject`), so the nav
104:   container is a plain `Item` whose pages the renderer manages (only the top
105:   visible) — a renderer-owned page cache, same statelessness contract.
106: 
107: ## Not implemented / gaps
108: 
109: - Pointer `hover`/`leave` flags (`POINTER_MOVE` hovering/leaving) and
110:   `KEY_DOWN`/`KEY_UP` listener bits are not yet reported; BackSpace as native
111:   back (text-focus detection) is deferred.
112: - The Rust DSL does not yet expose signal property bindings (the Java DSL
113:   does), so the demo marks the slider bound via a `BINDING_ID` on the retained
114:   tree; a real `.value(Signal)` DSL binding is a DSL/engine feature.
115: - The Rust DSL has no `NavigationContainer` either (the spec table is
116:   aspirational) — the renderer consumes ROUTE/NAV_DEPTH, but the Rust demo
117:   can't exercise nav without a DSL feature; Java/SplitNavDemo is the nav demo
118:   vehicle (Phase D).
119: - `TRANSITION`-hint animation, back-swipe gestures, multi-step deep-link
120:   intermediate pages (same gaps as the GTK renderer).
121: - `BACKGROUND_COLOR`/border on stacks/controls (Qt Quick Controls own their
122:   background delegate; mapping is a follow-up), `SHAPE` path approximation,
123:   `MENU` popup item list, `DATE_PICKER`/`COLOR_PICKER` native dialogs, and
124:   `PICKER` option styling not yet mapped.
125: - **FILL in Qt positioners**: `Row`/`Column`/`Grid` reject `anchors.fill` on
126:   their children, so a `WIDTH`/`HEIGHT` `FILL` inside a stack defers and is
127:   skipped (the positioner sizes it) — cross-axis stretch would need Qt Quick
128:   Layouts (`RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout`). Qt may print "Cannot specify ...
129:   anchors for items inside Row" notes for DSL FILL/alignment patterns; the UI
130:   renders regardless (this is a fidelity gap, not a crash).
131: - **Java JNA demo** (`lib/java/pathland-qt-demo`) runs the shared
132:   `SplitNavDemo` (incl. native navigation) via `pathland_qt_run_ring` — the
133:   cross-language nav demo vehicle, since the Rust DSL lacks a
134:   `NavigationContainer`.
135: - Lazy views render eagerly.
136: 
137: ## Verified by
138: 
139: `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` (needs Qt6 dev libs; offscreen for the FFI
140: tests) — the delta diff suite, the end-to-end FFI batch
141: (`command_batch_crosses_into_cpp_offscreen`), the **full pipeline**
142: (`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`: DSL → engine → frame → shared decode →
143: delta diff → FFI → live QML `Column`/`Text`/`Button`/`Slider` with spacing/value
144: applied and a delta re-applied), pointer-listener MouseArea attachment
145: (`pointer_listeners_attach_mousearea`), the event path
146: (`decode_maps_pointer_and_global_events`, `ring_event_writes_pointer_into_ring_and_wakes`,
147: `scheme_event_reapplies_without_waking`, `text_event_string_is_length_prefixed`,
148: `frame_has_reset_detects_meta_reset`), and Phase-B control coverage
149: (`control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, `picker_builds_model_from_option_children`),
150: and the nav adapter (`nav_slot_promotes_and_pushes_root_page`,
151: `nav_depth_push_and_pop`, `nav_replace_same_depth_new_route`,
152: `nav_custom_chrome_bare_pages`). Full workspace: `cd lib/rust && cargo test`.
153: Java JNA demo: `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` (headless `RingEventReaderTest`
154: runs in the Maven reactor; the live host mounts `SplitNavDemo`).
155: Demo: `scripts/run-rust-qt-demo.sh`.

(End of file - total 155 lines)
</content>

1: //! # pathland-render-qt
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **Qt Quick renderer**. It consumes opcode frames (via
4: //! `pathland_render_core::RenderTree`) and maps them **incrementally** onto a
5: //! Qt Quick scene graph — `Row`/`Column` for stacks, `Text` for text, Qt Quick
6: //! Controls for buttons/fields/sliders.
7: //!
8: //! The crate is split across languages on purpose:
9: //! - **Rust** owns the shared decode core (`pathland-render-core`), the
10: //!   sent-state **delta diff** ([`renderer::QtRenderer`]), the `Pump`
11: //!   transport seam, wire encoding, and the C ABI for foreign hosts
12: //!   ([`capi`]).
13: //! - **C++** (in `src/qt/`) owns the Qt application shell and maps the delta
14: //!   command batch onto QML items. It reports inputs back through a wake
15: //!   callback; the renderer **never drains events** — the host drains its own
16: //!   ring, symmetric with frames flowing in.
17: //!
18: //! The Qt layer is the only place that touches Qt; the protocol core
19: //! (`pathland-core`/`pathland-view`) stays `no_std`/wasm-safe.
20:

22: mod ffi;
23: pub mod renderer;

2: //
3: // Owns the Qt application objects (QGuiApplication / QQuickWindow / QQmlEngine /
4: // a root Item / the QML-facing Bridge) and applies the Rust delta command batch
5: // to QML items: create/delete/insert/remove widgets, set text + properties, and
6: // report control inputs back through the Bridge. The shell is split so tests
7: // can `init` the scene headless (offscreen) and drive `apply` without entering
8: // the event loop.

10: // Contract: the renderer never drains events — Rust encodes what the Bridge
11: // reports and wakes the host. Programmatic value sets suppress echoes, and only
12: // BINDING_ID/ACTION_ID-gated nodes report interactions (spec/EVENTS.md).

160:     // props arrived before they gained their final parent. Applied on insert
161:     // (skipped when the parent is a positioner — Row/Column reject anchors).
162:     std::unordered_map<QQuickItem *, uint8_t> pending_fill;

164:     bool suppress = false;

166:     // Test hooks: record what `apply` received.
167:     uint32_t apply_count = 0;

179: QQuickItem *createComponent(QQmlEngine *engine, QQuickItem *parent, const char *qml) {
180:     QQmlComponent comp(engine);
181:     comp.setData(QByteArray(qml), QUrl());
182:     if (comp.isError()) {
183:         qWarning() << "component error:" << comp.errorString();
184:         return nullptr;
185:     }
186:     QObject *obj = comp.create();
187:     if (!obj) {
188:         qWarning() << "create failed:" << comp.errorString();
189:         return nullptr;
190:     }
191:     QQuickItem *item = qobject_cast<QQuickItem *>(obj);
192:     if (item && parent) {
193:         item->setParentItem(parent);
194:     }
195:     return item;
196: }

313: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
314: // Navigation adapter (spec DSL.md §4.5): a VSTACK/HSTACK slot carrying ROUTE
315: // renders as a StackView; the adapter reconciles its page stack by NAV_DEPTH.

318: bool isStackComponent(uint16_t component) {
319:     return component == PL_COMP_VSTACK || component == PL_COMP_HSTACK ||
320:            component == PL_COMP_LAZY_VSTACK || component == PL_COMP_LAZY_HSTACK;
321: }

323: // Whether a parent item is a Qt Quick positioner (Row/Column/Grid). Positioners
324: // manage child placement themselves, so `anchors.fill` is rejected on their
325: // children — FILL there falls back to the positioner's default sizing.
326: bool isPositioner(QQuickItem *parent) {
327:     if (!parent) {
328:         return false;
329:     }
330:     const char *cls = parent->metaObject()->className();
331:     return cls && (strstr(cls, "QQuickRow") || strstr(cls, "QQuickColumn") ||
332:                    strstr(cls, "QQuickGrid"));
333: }
334: 
335: // The nav container: a plain Item page stack. Qt Quick has no native
336: // navigation container, and StackView's push/pop are QML-callable-only (not
337: // invokable from C++ via QMetaObject), so the renderer manages its page cache
338: // itself: pages are children of this Item, only the top is visible.
339: QQuickItem *createNavContainer(QQuickItem *parent) {
340:     return createComponent(g.engine, parent, "import QtQuick 2.15\nItem { clip: true }");
341: }
342: 
343: // Promote a slot's Column/Row to the nav container (first non-empty ROUTE).
344: // Children are inserted after props, so the slot has none yet — safe to swap.
345: void promoteNavSlot(uint32_t slotId) {
346:     auto it = g.widgets.find(slotId);
347:     if (it == g.widgets.end()) {
348:         return;
349:     }
350:     QQuickItem *old = it->second;
351:     QQuickItem *container = createNavContainer(old->parentItem());
352:     if (!container) {
353:         return;
354:     }
355:     // Fill the slot's parent when it is a plain container (a positioner like
356:     // Row/Column rejects anchors on its children and sizes them itself).
357:     if (old->parentItem() && !isPositioner(old->parentItem())) {
358:         QObject *anchors = container->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
359:         if (anchors) {
360:             anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(old->parentItem()));
361:         }
362:     }
363:     g.widgets[slotId] = container;
364:     g.nav_slots.insert(slotId);
365:     g.nav_stacks[slotId] = container;
366:     old->deleteLater();
367: }

380:             "    Row { id: header; height: showBack ? 32 : 0; visible: showBack\n"
381:             "      Button { text: \"\\u2190\"; onClicked: bridge.navigateBack() } }\n"
382:             "    Item { id: content; objectName: \"content\";\n"
383:             "      width: parent.width; height: parent.height - header.height } } }")
384:             .arg(isRoot ? "false" : "true")
385:             .toUtf8());

388: // Place a destination subtree root into a container, filling it.
389: void placeDestination(QQuickItem *dest, QQuickItem *container) {
390:     if (!dest || !container) {
391:         return;
392:     }
393:     g.pending_fill.erase(dest);
394:     dest->setParentItem(container);
395:     QObject *anchors = dest->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
396:     if (anchors) {
397:         anchors->setProperty("fill", QVariant::fromValue(container));
398:     }
399: }

401: // Reconcile a nav slot's page stack against the app's current destination
402: // (single child) + ROUTE + NAV_DEPTH, mirroring the GTK renderer's depth logic:
403: // pop down to depth, then Refresh (same route) / Push (deeper) / Replace
404: // (same depth, new route). The back-stack stays app-owned; this stack is the
405: // renderer's rendered-output cache. Only the top page is visible.
406: void reconcileNav(uint32_t slotId) {
407:     auto sit = g.nav_stacks.find(slotId);
408:     if (sit == g.nav_stacks.end()) {
409:         return;
410:     }
411:     QQuickItem *container = sit->second;
412:     auto rit = g.nav_route.find(slotId);
413:     const QString route = rit != g.nav_route.end() ? rit->second : QString();
414:     const uint32_t depth = std::max(g.nav_depth[slotId], 1u);
415:     const bool custom = g.nav_custom_chrome.count(slotId) > 0;
416: 
417:     // The destination subtree root: the slot's single child.
418:     QQuickItem *dest = nullptr;
419:     for (uint32_t childId : g.children_of[slotId]) {
420:         dest = findWidget(childId);
421:         if (dest) {
422:             break;
423:         }
424:     }
425: 
426:     auto &pages = g.nav_pages[slotId];
427:     auto &tags = g.nav_page_tags[slotId];
428: 
429:     // Pop down to the app's depth (renderer-driven; no NAVIGATE emitted).
430:     while (pages.size() > depth) {
431:         QQuickItem *page = pages.back();
432:         pages.pop_back();
433:         tags.pop_back();
434:         if (custom) {
435:             // The page IS the destination widget (app-owned); just detach it.
436:             page->setParentItem(nullptr);
437:             page->setVisible(false);
438:         } else {
439:             // Detach any destination the wrapper owns so the app-owned widget
440:             // survives the wrapper's destruction.
441:             if (QQuickItem *c = page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content")) {
442:                 const auto kids = c->childItems();
443:                 for (QQuickItem *kid : kids) {
444:                     kid->setParentItem(nullptr);
445:                 }
446:             }
447:             page->setParentItem(nullptr);
448:             page->deleteLater();
449:         }
450:     }
451: 
452:     auto showTop = [&]() {
453:         for (size_t i = 0; i < pages.size(); ++i) {
454:             pages[i]->setVisible(i + 1 == pages.size());
455:         }
456:     };
457: 
458:     if (pages.empty()) {
459:         if (custom && !dest) {
460:             return; // nothing to show yet (reconcile re-fires on the child)
461:         }
462:         QQuickItem *page = custom ? dest : navPageWrapper(/*isRoot=*/true);
463:         if (custom) {
464:             placeDestination(dest, container);
465:         } else if (dest) {
466:             placeDestination(dest, page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
467:             page->setParentItem(container);
468:         } else {
469:             page->setParentItem(container);
470:         }
471:         page->setVisible(true);
472:         pages.push_back(page);
473:         tags.push_back(route);
474:         return;
475:     }
476: 
477:     QQuickItem *top = pages.back();
478:     const QString topTag = tags.back();
479:     if (topTag == route) {
480:         // Refresh in place (signal update / re-emit after a user back).
481:         if (!custom && dest) {
482:             placeDestination(dest, top->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
483:         }
484:     } else if (pages.size() < depth) {
485:         // Deeper -> push a new page.
486:         if (custom && !dest) {
487:             return;
488:         }
489:         QQuickItem *page = custom ? dest : navPageWrapper(/*isRoot=*/false);
490:         if (custom) {
491:             placeDestination(dest, container);
492:         } else if (dest) {
493:             placeDestination(dest, page->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
494:             page->setParentItem(container);
495:         } else {
496:             page->setParentItem(container);
497:         }
498:         if (top != page) {
499:             top->setVisible(false);
500:         }
501:         page->setVisible(true);
502:         pages.push_back(page);
503:         tags.push_back(route);
504:     } else {
505:         // Same depth, new route -> replace the top page's content.
506:         if (custom) {
507:             if (dest && dest != top) {
508:                 top->setParentItem(nullptr);
509:                 placeDestination(dest, container);
510:                 dest->setVisible(true);
511:                 pages.back() = dest;
512:             }
513:         } else if (dest) {
514:             placeDestination(dest, top->findChild<QQuickItem *>("content"));
515:         }
516:         tags.back() = route;
517:     }
518:     showTop();
519: }

521: // Remove a node's EVENT_LISTENERS MouseArea overlay (if any).
522: void detachPointerArea(uint32_t id) {
523:     auto it = g.mouse_areas.find(id);
524:     if (it != g.mouse_areas.end()) {
525:         it->second->deleteLater();
526:         g.mouse_areas.erase(it);
527:     }
528:     g.listener_masks.erase(id);
529: }

531: // Attach a MouseArea overlay for a node's EVENT_LISTENERS pointer mask. Only
532: // the requested handler kinds are wired (each already gated by the mask), so
533: // the Bridge's pointer path needs no extra gating.
534: void attachPointerArea(uint32_t id, uint32_t mask) {
535:     detachPointerArea(id);
536:     const uint32_t bits = mask & (1 | 2 | 4); // POINTER_DOWN | POINTER_MOVE | POINTER_UP
537:     if (bits == 0) {
538:         return;
539:     }
540:     QQuickItem *item = findWidget(id);
541:     if (!item) {
542:         return;
543:     }
544:     QString handlers;
545:     if (mask & 1) { // POINTER_DOWN -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_DOWN = 4
546:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onPressed: bridge.pointer(%1, 4, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
547:     }
548:     if (mask & 2) { // POINTER_MOVE -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_MOVE = 5
549:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onPositionChanged: bridge.pointer(%1, 5, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
550:     }
551:     if (mask & 4) { // POINTER_UP -> PLQT_EV_POINTER_UP = 1
552:         handlers += QStringLiteral("onReleased: bridge.pointer(%1, 1, mouse.x, mouse.y)\n").arg(id);
553:     }
554:     const QString qml =
555:         QStringLiteral("import QtQuick 2.15\nMouseArea { anchors.fill: parent;\n%1}").arg(handlers);
556:     QQuickItem *area = createComponent(g.engine, item, qml.toUtf8());
557:     if (area) {
558:         g.mouse_areas[id] = area;
559:         g.listener_masks[id] = mask;
560:     }
561: }

563: // Pathland cross-axis alignment (0=Start,1=Center,2=End,else Fill) -> Qt's
564: // Row/Column `align` (Qt 6.7+, horizontal flags for a Column).
565: int alignFor(uint32_t raw) {
566:     const float f = f32(raw);
567:     const int idx = (std::isfinite(f) && std::floor(f) == f && f >= 0.0f && f <= 3.0f)
568:                         ? static_cast<int>(f)
569:                         : static_cast<int>(raw & 0xFF);
570:     switch (idx) {
571:     case 0:
572:         return Qt::AlignLeft; // Start
573:     case 1:
574:         return Qt::AlignHCenter; // Center
575:     case 2:
576:         return Qt::AlignRight; // End
577:     default:
578:         return Qt::AlignLeft; // Fill -> stretch is the QML default; gap
579:     }
580: }
581: 
582: int weightFor(float weight) {
583:     const int w = static_cast<int>(weight + 0.5f);
584:     switch (w) {
585:     case 100:
586:         return int(QFont::Thin);
587:     case 200:
588:         return int(QFont::ExtraLight);
589:     case 300:
590:         return int(QFont::Light);
591:     case 500:
592:         return int(QFont::Medium);
593:     case 600:
594:         return int(QFont::DemiBold);
595:     case 700:
596:         return int(QFont::Bold);
597:     case 800:
598:         return int(QFont::ExtraBold);
599:     case 900:
600:         return int(QFont::Black);
601:     default:
602:         return int(QFont::Normal);
603:     }
604: }

606: // WIDTH/HEIGHT special values: -1 = FILL (anchors.fill parent), -2 = HUG
607: // (implicit size). Positive values set an explicit size.
608: // Apply a pending FILL (anchors.fill) once a widget gains its final parent.
609: // Skipped for positioners (Row/Column/Grid reject anchors on their children).
610: void flushFill(QQuickItem *item, QQuickItem *container) {
611:     auto it = g.pending_fill.find(item);
612:     if (it == g.pending_fill.end()) {
613:         return;
614:     }
615:     if (container && !isPositioner(container)) {
616:         QObject *anchors = item->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
617:         if (anchors) {
618:             if (it->second & 1u) {
619:                 anchors->setProperty("width", QVariant::fromValue(container));
620:             }
621:             if (it->second & 2u) {
622:                 anchors->setProperty("height", QVariant::fromValue(container));
623:             }
624:         }
625:     }
626:     g.pending_fill.erase(it);
627: }
628: 
629: void applySize(QQuickItem *item, const char *dimension, float value) {
630:     if (value == -1.0f) {
631:         // FILL: apply once the widget is in its final parent. Props arrive
632:         // before children are inserted, so if the parent is unknown (or a
633:         // positioner that rejects anchors) defer to insert time.
634:         QQuickItem *parent = item->parentItem();
635:         if (parent && !isPositioner(parent)) {
636:             QObject *anchors = item->property("anchors").value<QObject *>();
637:             if (anchors) {
638:                 anchors->setProperty(dimension, QVariant::fromValue(parent));
639:             }
640:         } else {
641:             g.pending_fill[item] |= (*dimension == 'w') ? 1u : 2u;
642:         }
643:         return;
644:     }
645:     if (value == -2.0f) {
646:         return; // HUG_CONTENT: implicit size is the default
647:     }
648:     item->setProperty(dimension, static_cast<double>(value));
649: }

651: void applyProperty(uint32_t id, uint16_t prop, uint8_t value_type, uint32_t value) {
652:     QQuickItem *item = findWidget(id);
653:     if (!item) {
654:         return;
655:     }
656:     switch (prop) {
657:     case PL_PROP_SPACING:
658:         item->setProperty("spacing", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
659:         break;
660:     case PL_PROP_ALIGNMENT:
661:         item->setProperty("align", alignFor(value));
662:         break;
663:     case PL_PROP_PADDING:
664:         item->setProperty("padding", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
665:         break;
666:     case PL_PROP_PADDING_TOP:
667:         item->setProperty("topPadding", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
668:         break;
669:     case PL_PROP_PADDING_RIGHT:
670:         item->setProperty("rightPadding", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
671:         break;
672:     case PL_PROP_PADDING_BOTTOM:
673:         item->setProperty("bottomPadding", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
674:         break;
675:     case PL_PROP_PADDING_LEFT:
676:         item->setProperty("leftPadding", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
677:         break;
678:     case PL_PROP_WIDTH:
679:         applySize(item, "width", f32(value));
680:         break;
681:     case PL_PROP_HEIGHT:
682:         applySize(item, "height", f32(value));
683:         break;
684:     case PL_PROP_COLOR:
685:         item->setProperty("color", QColor::fromRgba(value));
686:         break;
687:     case PL_PROP_FONT_SIZE:
688:         item->setProperty("font.pixelSize", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
689:         break;
690:     case PL_PROP_FONT_WEIGHT:
691:         item->setProperty("font.weight", weightFor(f32(value)));
692:         break;
693:     case PL_PROP_OPACITY:
694:         item->setProperty("opacity", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
695:         break;
696:     case PL_PROP_VISIBLE:
697:         item->setProperty("visible", value != 0);
698:         break;
699:     case PL_PROP_Z_INDEX:
700:         item->setProperty("z", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
701:         break;
702:     case PL_PROP_VALUE:
703:         item->setProperty("value", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
704:         break;
705:     case PL_PROP_MIN:
706:         item->setProperty("from", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
707:         break;
708:     case PL_PROP_MAX:
709:         item->setProperty("to", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
710:         break;
711:     case PL_PROP_STEP:
712:         item->setProperty("stepSize", static_cast<double>(f32(value)));
713:         break;
714:     case PL_PROP_SELECTED:
715:         item->setProperty("checked", value != 0);

808: // Rebuild a PICKER's ComboBox model from its ordered option children's text.
809: void rebuildPickerModel(uint32_t parentId) {
810:     auto cit = g.components.find(parentId);
811:     if (cit == g.components.end() || cit->second != PL_COMP_PICKER) {
812:         return;
813:     }
814:     QQuickItem *picker = findWidget(parentId);
815:     if (!picker) {
816:         return;
817:     }
818:     QStringList model;
819:     for (uint32_t optId : g.children_of[parentId]) {
820:         QQuickItem *opt = findWidget(optId);
821:         model << (opt ? opt->property("text").toString() : QString());
822:     }
823:     picker->setProperty("model", model);

826: void insertChild(uint32_t parentId, uint32_t childId, uint32_t index) {
827:     QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
828:     if (!child) {
829:         return;
830:     }
831:     g.parents[childId] = parentId;
832:     // Maintain the ordered structural mirror for every parent.
833:     auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
834:     siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
835:     if (index == UINT32_MAX || index >= siblings.size()) {
836:         siblings.push_back(childId);
837:     } else {
838:         siblings.insert(siblings.begin() + index, childId);
839:     }
840: 
841:     if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
842:         rebuildPickerModel(parentId); // options drive the model, not the visual tree
843:         return;
844:     }
845:     if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
846:         reconcileNav(parentId); // destination subtree swap -> refresh/replace the top page
847:         return; // the destination is placed by the nav adapter, not visually here
848:     }
849: 
850:     QQuickItem *parent = findWidget(parentId);
851:     if (!parent) {
852:         return;
853:     }
854:     child->setParentItem(parent);
855:     flushFill(child, parent);
856:     if (index == UINT32_MAX) {
857:         return; // append (already last)
858:     }
859:     QList<QQuickItem *> siblingsList = parent->childItems();
860:     siblingsList.removeAll(child);
861:     if (static_cast<int>(index) < siblingsList.size()) {
862:         QQuickItem *after = siblingsList.at(static_cast<int>(index));
863:         if (after != child) {
864:             child->stackBefore(after);
865:         }
866:     }
867: }

900: class KeyFilter : public QObject {
901: public:

1002: void pathland_qt_layer_apply(const PathlandQtCommand *cmds, uint32_t count) {
1003:     if (!g.initialized || !cmds || count == 0) {
1004:         return;
1005:     }
1006:     for (uint32_t i = 0; i < count; ++i) {
1007:         const PathlandQtCommand &c = cmds[i];
1008:         switch (c.kind) {
1009:         case PLQT_CREATE_NODE: {
1010:             const uint16_t component = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
1011:             QQuickItem *item = createComponent(g.engine, g.root, qmlFor(component, c.a).toUtf8());
1012:             if (item) {
1013:                 g.widgets[c.a] = item;
1014:                 g.components[c.a] = component;
1015:             }
1016:             break;
1017:         }
1018:         case PLQT_DELETE_NODE:
1019:             deleteNode(c.a);
1020:             break;
1021:         case PLQT_INSERT_CHILD:
1022:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c);
1023:             break;
1024:         case PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD: {
1025:             const uint32_t parentId = c.a;
1026:             const uint32_t childId = c.b;
1027:             g.parents.erase(childId);
1028:             auto &siblings = g.children_of[parentId];
1029:             siblings.erase(std::remove(siblings.begin(), siblings.end(), childId), siblings.end());
1030:             if (g.components[parentId] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
1031:                 rebuildPickerModel(parentId);
1032:             } else if (g.nav_slots.count(parentId)) {
1033:                 reconcileNav(parentId);
1034:             } else {
1035:                 QQuickItem *child = findWidget(childId);
1036:                 if (child) {
1037:                     child->setParentItem(nullptr); // keep alive (may be reinserted)
1038:                 }
1039:             }
1040:             break;
1041:         }
1042:         case PLQT_MOVE_CHILD:
1043:             insertChild(c.a, c.b, c.c); // reorder == reinsert at index
1044:             break;
1045:         case PLQT_SET_TEXT: {
1046:             QQuickItem *item = findWidget(c.a);
1047:             if (item && c.str) {
1048:                 g.suppress = true;
1049:                 item->setProperty("text", QString::fromUtf8(c.str, static_cast<int>(c.str_len)));
1050:                 g.suppress = false;
1051:             }
1052:             // A picker option's label feeds its parent's ComboBox model.
1053:             auto pit = g.parents.find(c.a);
1054:             if (pit != g.parents.end() && g.components[pit->second] == PL_COMP_PICKER) {
1055:                 rebuildPickerModel(pit->second);
1056:             }
1057:             // Record for the test hook.
1058:             if (c.str && c.str_len > 0) {
1059:                 const uint32_t n = c.str_len < sizeof(g.last_text) - 1 ? c.str_len
1060:                                                                        : sizeof(g.last_text) - 1;
1061:                 std::memcpy(g.last_text, c.str, n);
1062:                 g.last_text[n] = '\0';
1063:                 g.last_text_len = n;
1064:             }
1065:             break;
1066:         }
1067:         case PLQT_SET_PROPERTY: {
1068:             const uint16_t prop = static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b & 0xFFFF);
1069:             const uint8_t vt = static_cast<uint8_t>((c.b >> 16) & 0xFF);
1070:             g.suppress = true;
1071:             applyProperty(c.a, prop, vt, c.c);
1072:             g.suppress = false;
1073:             break;
1074:         }
1075:         case PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY:
1076:             g.suppress = true;
1077:             applyStringProperty(c.a, static_cast<uint16_t>(c.b), c.str, c.str_len);
1078:             g.suppress = false;
1079:             break;
1080:         case PLQT_RESET_NODE:
1081:             resetNode(c.a);
1082:             break;
1083:         case PLQT_SET_SCHEME:
1084:             break; // MVP: scheme handling is a follow-up
1085:         }
1086:     }
1087:     g.apply_count += count;

88:         let mut cmds = Vec::new();
89: 
90:         // 1. Deletions first: nodes gone from the tree.
91:         let live: HashSet<u32> = self.tree.nodes.keys().copied().collect();
92:         let dead: Vec<u32> = self
93:             .sent
94:             .keys()
95:             .copied()
96:             .filter(|id| !live.contains(id))
97:             .collect();
98:         for id in dead {
99:             cmds.push(Command::delete_node(id));
100:             self.sent.remove(&id);
101:             self.sent_children.remove(&id);
102:         }
103: 
104:         // 2. Creates (pre-order, so a parent exists before its children are
105:         //    inserted, and a child before any insert references it).
106:         let order = self.pre_order();
107:         for &id in &order {
108:             if self.sent.contains_key(&id) {
109:                 continue;
110:             }
111:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
112:             cmds.push(Command::create_node(id, node.component_type));
113:             self.sent.insert(
114:                 id,
115:                 SentNode::default(),
116:             );
117:         }
118: 
119:         // 3. Text + property deltas. On any property change we re-send the
120:         //    node's *complete* property set (preceded by RESET_NODE), so the
121:         //    C++ layer can reset removed properties to its renderer defaults.
122:         for &id in &order {
123:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
124:             let s = self.sent.get_mut(&id).unwrap();
125: 
126:             if s.text != node.text {
127:                 cmds.push(Command::set_text(id, node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")));
128:                 s.text = node.text.clone();
129:             }
130:             if node.properties != s.props || node.strings != s.strings {
131:                 cmds.push(Command::reset_node(id));
132:                 // Emit numeric props in a deterministic order with VALUE last:
133:                 // Qt Quick clamps a control's `value` when `from`/`to` aren't
134:                 // configured yet, so min/max must land before the value.
135:                 let mut props: Vec<(u16, u32)> =
136:                     node.properties.iter().map(|(k, v)| (*k, *v)).collect();
137:                 props.sort_by_key(|(p, _)| (*p == pathland_core::property_id::VALUE, *p));
138:                 for (prop, value) in &props {
139:                     let vt = value_type_for(*prop);
140:                     cmds.push(Command::set_property(id, *prop, vt, *value));
141:                 }
142:                 for (prop, value) in &node.strings {
143:                     cmds.push(Command::set_string_property(id, *prop, value));
144:                 }
145:                 s.props = node.properties.clone();
146:                 s.strings = node.strings.clone();
147:             }
148:         }
149: 
150:         // 4. Child order (parents before children already exist). The shared
151:         //    core's DELETE_NODE leaves a ghost in the parent's child list, so
152:         //    filter to live nodes before diffing.
153:         for &id in &order {
154:             let node = self.tree.node(id).unwrap();
155:             let children: Vec<u32> = node
156:                 .children
157:                 .iter()
158:                 .copied()
159:                 .filter(|c| self.tree.nodes.contains_key(c))
160:                 .collect();
161:             let prev = self.sent_children.entry(id).or_default();
162:             cmds.extend(children_diff(id, prev, &children));
163:             *prev = children;
164:         }
165: 
166:         // 5. Roots are children of the pseudo-parent 0 (window contentItem).
167:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = order
168:             .iter()
169:             .copied()
170:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
171:             .collect();
172:         roots.sort_unstable();
173:         let prev_roots = self.sent_children.entry(CONTENT_ITEM).or_default();
174:         cmds.extend(children_diff(CONTENT_ITEM, prev_roots, &roots));
175:         *prev_roots = roots;
176: 
177:         cmds
178:     }
179: 
180:     fn pre_order(&self) -> Vec<u32> {
181:         let mut order = Vec::new();
182:         let mut roots: Vec<u32> = self
183:             .tree
184:             .nodes
185:             .keys()
186:             .copied()
187:             .filter(|&id| self.tree.node(id).map_or(false, |n| n.parent.is_none()))
188:             .collect();
189:         roots.sort_unstable();
190:         for r in roots {
191:             self.walk(r, &mut order);
192:         }
193:         order
194:     }
195: 
196:     fn walk(&self, id: u32, out: &mut Vec<u32>) {
197:         // Guard against ghost children (a node deleted from `tree.nodes` but
198:         // still listed in a parent's `children` after DELETE_NODE).
199:         if !self.tree.nodes.contains_key(&id) {
200:             return;
201:         }
202:         out.push(id);
203:         if let Some(node) = self.tree.node(id) {
204:             for c in node.children.clone() {
205:                 self.walk(c, out);
206:             }
207:         }
208:     }
209: }

211: /// The opcode wire's value type for a property (same mapping the emit side
212: /// uses; the C++ layer needs it to interpret the raw u32).
213: fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
214:     if is_f32_property(prop) {
215:         value_type::F32
216:     } else {
217:         value_type::U32
218:     }
219: }
220: 
221: fn is_f32_property(prop: u16) -> bool {
222:     matches!(
223:         prop,
224:         pathland_core::property_id::SPACING
225:             | pathland_core::property_id::WIDTH
226:             | pathland_core::property_id::HEIGHT
227:             | pathland_core::property_id::FONT_SIZE
228:             | pathland_core::property_id::OPACITY
229:             | pathland_core::property_id::BORDER_WIDTH
230:             | pathland_core::property_id::BORDER_RADIUS
231:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING
232:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_TOP
233:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_RIGHT
234:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_BOTTOM
235:             | pathland_core::property_id::PADDING_LEFT
236:             | pathland_core::property_id::VALUE
237:             | pathland_core::property_id::MIN_VALUE
238:             | pathland_core::property_id::MAX_VALUE
239:             | pathland_core::property_id::STEP_VALUE
240:             | pathland_core::property_id::PROGRESS
241:             | pathland_core::property_id::NAV_CHROME
242:             | pathland_core::property_id::TRANSITION
243:     )
244: }
245: 
246: /// Minimal child-order delta: for each index where the old and new children
247: /// differ, remove the stale child and insert the new one at that index.
248: fn children_diff(parent: u32, prev: &[u32], next: &[u32]) -> Vec<Command> {
249:     let mut cmds = Vec::new();
250:     let len = prev.len().max(next.len());
251:     for i in 0..len {
252:         let old = prev.get(i).copied();
253:         let new = next.get(i).copied();
254:         if old == new {
255:             continue;
256:         }
257:         if let Some(c) = old {
258:             cmds.push(Command::remove_child(parent, c));
259:         }
260:         if let Some(c) = new {
261:             cmds.push(Command::insert_child(parent, c, i as u32));
262:         }
263:     }
264:     cmds
265: }

274:     /// One persistent engine + ring memory, so consecutive emits are **deltas**
275:     /// (like a live app) rather than full snapshots.
276:     struct Harness {
277:         layout: MemoryLayout,
278:         mem: Vec<u8>,
279:         engine: Engine,

281: 
282:     impl Harness {
283:         fn new() -> Self {
284:             let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
285:             let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
286:             init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
287:             Self {
288:                 layout,
289:                 mem,
290:                 engine: Engine::new(),
291:             }
292:         }

294:         /// Emit `root` (delta against the previous emit) and return the frame's
295:         /// slots + arena copied into owned buffers (`frame spans 0..len`).
296:         /// An unchanged tree emits **zero** opcodes (returns empty buffers).
297:         fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
298:             let layout = self.layout;
299:             {
300:                 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
301:                 guest.begin_frame();
302:                 self.engine.emit(root, &mut guest).unwrap();
303:                 guest.end_frame();
304:             }
305:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
306:             let frames = host.frames();
307:             assert!(frames.len() <= 1, "at most one frame per emit");
308:             let Some(f) = frames.first() else {
309:                 return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
310:             };
311:             let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(f.len() * 16);
312:             for op in f.opcodes() {
313:                 slots.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
314:             }
315:             let arena = f.arena().to_vec();
316:             (slots, arena)
317:         }
318:     }

320:     fn apply_emit(r: &mut QtRenderer, h: &mut Harness, root: &Node) {
321:         let (slots, arena) = h.emit(root);
322:         let frame = Frame::from_parts(&slots, &arena, 0, slots.len());
323:         r.tree.apply_frame(&frame);
324:     }

2: //! entry points, and the test hooks. Mirrors `src/qt/pathland_qt.h`.

4: //! A [`Command`] is one delta — Rust produces a batch (the engine's "only
5: //! changes" discipline) and the C++ layer applies it to the Qt Quick scene.

10: /// One delta command handed to the C++ Qt layer. `str_` points into the
11: /// renderer's `RenderTree` strings and is only valid for the duration of the
12: /// enclosing [`crate::renderer::QtRenderer::apply_frame`] call.
13: #[repr(C)]
14: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy)]
15: pub struct Command {
16:     pub kind: u8,
17:     pub a: u32,
18:     pub b: u32,
19:     pub c: u32,
20:     pub str_len: u32,
21:     pub str_: *const c_char,
22: }

24: impl Command {
25:     pub const CREATE_NODE: u8 = 0;
26:     pub const DELETE_NODE: u8 = 1;
27:     pub const INSERT_CHILD: u8 = 2;
28:     pub const REMOVE_CHILD: u8 = 3;
29:     pub const MOVE_CHILD: u8 = 4;
30:     pub const SET_TEXT: u8 = 5;
31:     pub const SET_PROPERTY: u8 = 6;

42:             str_len: 0,

176: /// Forward a command batch to the C++ layer.
177: pub fn apply(cmds: &[Command]) {
178:     if cmds.is_empty() {
179:         return;
180:     }
181:     // SAFETY: `cmds` strings point into the renderer's `RenderTree`, which is
182:     // not mutated during the call (same `apply_frame` borrow).
183:     unsafe { pathland_qt_layer_apply(cmds.as_ptr(), cmds.len() as u32) };
184: }

222:     /// One persistent engine + ring memory, so consecutive emits are deltas.
223:     struct Harness {

229:     impl Harness {
230:         fn new() -> Self {
231:             let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
232:             let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
233:             init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
234:             Self {
235:                 layout,

241:         fn emit(&mut self, root: &Node) -> (Vec<u8>, Vec<u8>) {
242:             let layout = self.layout;
243:             {
244:                 let mut guest = Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
245:                 guest.begin_frame();
246:                 self.engine.emit(root, &mut guest).unwrap();
247:                 guest.end_frame();
248:             }
249:             let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &layout);
250:             let frames = host.frames();
251:             let Some(f) = frames.first() else {
252:                 return (Vec::new(), Vec::new());
253:             };
254:             let mut slots = Vec::with_capacity(f.len() * 16);
255:             for op in f.opcodes() {
256:                 slots.extend_from_slice(&op.to_bytes());
257:             }
258:             let arena = f.arena().to_vec();
259:             (slots, arena)
260:         }
261:     }

1: // Shared C ABI types between the Rust decode core and the C++ Qt widget layer.
2: //
3: // A `PathlandQtCommand` is one delta: Rust produces a batch (mirroring the
4: // opcode engine's "only changes" discipline) and C++ applies it to the Qt Quick
5: // scene. This is deliberately a flat struct — the renderer's FFI boundary stays
6: // a batch of small commands, never a serialized tree.
7: //
8: // Inputs flow back the same way: a `PathlandQtEvent` carries one raw input
9: // (control signal -> C++ -> Rust, which encodes the EVENT opcode and wakes the
10: // host). The renderer never drains events.
11: #ifndef PATHLAND_QT_LAYER_H
12: #define PATHLAND_QT_LAYER_H
13: 
14: #include <stdint.h>
15: #include <stddef.h>
16: 
17: #ifdef __cplusplus
18: extern "C" {
19: #endif
20: 
21: typedef enum PathlandQtCommandKind {
22:     PLQT_CREATE_NODE = 0,   /* a=id, b=componentType(u16 low)                    */
23:     PLQT_DELETE_NODE = 1,   /* a=id                                              */
24:     PLQT_INSERT_CHILD = 2,  /* a=parent, b=child, c=index (u32::MAX = append)    */
25:     PLQT_REMOVE_CHILD = 3,  /* a=parent, b=child                                 */
26:     PLQT_MOVE_CHILD = 4,    /* a=parent, b=child, c=newIndex                     */
27:     PLQT_SET_TEXT = 5,      /* a=id, str=text                                    */
28:     PLQT_SET_PROPERTY = 6,  /* a=id, b=(valueType<<16)|propertyId, c=value       */
29:     PLQT_SET_STRING_PROPERTY = 7, /* a=id, b=propertyId, str=value              */
30:     PLQT_RESET_NODE = 8,    /* a=id — reset renderer-owned style to defaults     */
31:     PLQT_SET_SCHEME = 9,    /* a=scheme (0 light, 1 dark)                        */
32: } PathlandQtCommandKind;
33: 
34: typedef struct PathlandQtCommand {
35:     uint8_t kind;
36:     uint32_t a;
37:     uint32_t b;
38:     uint32_t c;
39:     uint32_t str_len;
40:     const char *str;
41: } PathlandQtCommand;

43: /* One raw input reported by the Qt layer (C++ -> Rust). */
44: typedef enum PathlandQtEventKind {
45:     PLQT_EV_NONE = 0,
46:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_UP = 1,   /* a control was tapped / pointer released (x,y)   */
47:     PLQT_EV_VALUE_CHANGED = 2, /* a control's semantic value changed (f32)      */
48:     PLQT_EV_TEXT_CHANGED = 3, /* a text field's value changed (str)             */
49:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_DOWN = 4, /* pointer pressed on a listener node (x,y)       */
50:     PLQT_EV_POINTER_MOVE = 5, /* pointer moved on a listener node (x,y)         */
51:     PLQT_EV_NAVIGATE_BACK = 6, /* native back request (Escape), global           */
52:     PLQT_EV_SCHEME_CHANGED = 7, /* platform color scheme changed (value 0/1)     */
53: } PathlandQtEventKind;

56:     uint8_t kind;
57:     uint32_t node_id;
58:     float x;
59:     float y;
60:     float value;
61:     uint32_t str_len;
62:     const char *str;

65: /* Wake callback into the Rust host: an event was written to the ring; the host
66:    drains its own event ring (renderer never drains). */
67: typedef void (*PathlandQtWake)(void *user);

1: //! # Pathland Qt Quick desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native Qt Quick app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory
4: //! ring** and the shared **Qt renderer** (`pathland-render-qt`).
5: //!
6: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the diff emitter
7: //! emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into the shared ring, and the Qt renderer
8: //! maps them onto a Qt Quick scene (Row/Column/Text/Button/TextField/Slider).
9: //! The demo never touches Qt APIs directly — it only drives Pathland and the
10: //! renderer.
11: //!
12: //! Interaction is declared with `.on_tap_gesture(...)` on any view; raw pointer
13: //! events round-trip through the shared ring and are turned back into taps by
14: //! the app-side [`TapRecognizer`](pathland_view::TapRecognizer).
15: 
16: use std::cell::RefCell;
17: use std::collections::BTreeMap;
18: use std::rc::Rc;
19: use std::time::Instant;
20: 
21: use pathland_engine::Engine;
22: use pathland_core::listener;
23: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
24: use pathland_view::{
25:     assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Color, Node, Slider, View, ViewExt,
26: };
27: 
28: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.QtDemo";
29: 
30: /// node id → tap callback, collected from the built tree after `assign_ids`.
31: type TapHandlers = BTreeMap<u32, Rc<RefCell<dyn FnMut() + 'static>>>;
32: 
33: /// Mark a node as a value-reporting control (`BINDING_ID`), so the renderer
34: /// gates its `VALUE_CHANGED` events back to the app. The Rust DSL does not yet
35: /// expose signal property bindings, so the demo marks the slider directly on
36: /// the retained tree (the protocol's "this node reports" marker).
37: fn mark_value_bound(node: &mut Node) {
38:     if node.component == pathland_view::Component::Slider {
39:         node.properties
40:             .insert(pathland_core::property_id::BINDING_ID, 1);
41:     }
42:     for child in &mut node.children {
43:         mark_value_bound(child);
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter + slider value. This is the
48: /// developer's authoring surface.
49: fn build_tree(count: &Rc<RefCell<u32>>, slider_value: &Rc<RefCell<f32>>) -> Node {
50:     let tap_count = count.clone();
51:     let mut tree = vstack![
52:         hstack![
53:             text(format!("Count: {}", *count.borrow()).as_str()),
54:             button("Increment").on_tap_gesture(move || *tap_count.borrow_mut() += 1),
55:         ]
56:         .spacing(8.0)
57:         .padding(16.0),
58:         text("Pathland · Qt Quick · shared ring").foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_888888)),
59:         // A non-button view (Text) declaring raw pointer listeners — proving any
60:         // element can emit events via the `EVENT_LISTENERS` property.
61:         text("I am a Text with raw pointer listeners")
62:             .pointer_events(listener::POINTER_DOWN | listener::POINTER_UP)
63:             .foreground_style(Color::argb(0xFF_0000AA)),
64:         text(format!("Slider: {:.1}", *slider_value.borrow()).as_str()),
65:         Slider {
66:             value: *slider_value.borrow(),
67:             min: 0.0,
68:             max: 10.0,
69:         },
70:         vstack![
71:             text("short"),
72:             text("a much longer label"),
73:             text("x"),
74:         ]
75:         .spacing(4.0)
76:         .padding(16.0),
77:     ]
78:     .spacing(12.0)
79:     .padding(24.0)
80:     .build();
81:     mark_value_bound(&mut tree);
82:     tree
83: }
84: 
85: fn main() {
86:     let engine = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Engine::new()));
87:     let ring = Rc::new(RefCell::new(RingTransport::new()));
88:     let count = Rc::new(RefCell::new(0u32));
89:     let slider_value = Rc::new(RefCell::new(5.0f32));
90:     let handlers = Rc::new(RefCell::new(TapHandlers::new()));
91: 
92:     // Build + emit the current tree, refreshing the id → tap-callback map.
93:     let emit = {
94:         let engine = engine.clone();
95:         let ring = ring.clone();
96:         let count = count.clone();
97:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
98:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
99:         move || {
100:             let mut tree = build_tree(&count, &slider_value);
101:             assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
102:             let mut h = handlers.borrow_mut();
103:             h.clear();
104:             pathland_view::collect_tap_handlers(&tree, &mut *h);
105:             drop(h);
106: 
107:             let mut ring_ref = ring.borrow_mut();
108:             let mut guest = ring_ref.producer();
109:             guest.begin_frame();
110:             engine.borrow_mut().emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
111:             guest.end_frame();
112:         }
113:     };
114: 
115:     // Initial frame before the renderer starts pumping.
116:     emit();
117: 
118:     // Hand the renderer the shared ring and a wake handler. The renderer writes
119:     // native inputs as EVENT opcodes into the ring and wakes us; we drain the
120:     // ring, run the taps through the recognizer, invoke the matching callback,
121:     // and re-emit. The renderer's idle pump applies the delta.
122:     pathland_qt::run(APP_ID, "Pathland Qt Demo", ring.clone(), {
123:         let emit = emit;
124:         let handlers = handlers.clone();
125:         let slider_value = slider_value.clone();
126:         let start = Instant::now();
127:         let mut recognizer = pathland_view::TapRecognizer::new();
128:         move |ring| {
129:             let events = ring.borrow_mut().drain_events();
130:             let now_ms = start.elapsed().as_millis() as u64;
131:             let mut changed = false;
132:             for ev in &events {
133:                 // Platform back (Escape/back key) arrives as a global NAVIGATE
134:                 // request with no URL. There is no Rust router yet, so this is
135:                 // surfaced to the console to prove the event reached the app.
136:                 if matches!(ev, pathland_core::Event::Navigate { url: None }) {
137:                     eprintln!("[demo] NAVIGATE back requested");
138:                 }
139:                 // A bound control's value changed (the slider): update the app
140:                 // state and re-emit — the echo-suppressed, VALUE-last renderer
141:                 // path applies it back without a loop.
142:                 if let pathland_core::Event::ValueChanged { value, .. } = ev {
143:                     *slider_value.borrow_mut() = *value;
144:                     changed = true;
145:                 }
146:                 if let Some(target) = recognizer.feed(ev, now_ms) {
147:                     if let Some(handler) = handlers.borrow().get(&target) {
148:                         let mut cb = handler.borrow_mut();
149:                         (&mut *cb)();
150:                         changed = true;
151:                     }
152:                 }
153:             }
154:             if changed {
155:                 emit();
156:             }
157:         }
158:     });
159: }

18: public final class RingEventReader {
19: 
20:     private static final int OPCODE_SIZE = 16;
21:     private static final int CATEGORY_EVENT = 0x03;
22: 
23:     /** Ring header: byte offset of the event-arena offset (spec/OPCODE.md, memory.rs). */
24:     private static final int OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET = 0x40;
25: 
26:     private final Pointer ringPtr;
27:     private final long ringLen;
28:     private final int eventArenaOffset;
29: 
30:     public RingEventReader(Pointer ringPtr, long ringLen) {
31:         this.ringPtr = ringPtr;
32:         this.ringLen = ringLen;
33:         if (ringPtr != null && ringLen >= OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET + 4L) {
34:             this.eventArenaOffset = ringPtr.getInt(OFF_EVENT_ARENA_OFFSET);
35:         } else {
36:             this.eventArenaOffset = 0;
37:         }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /** Decode consecutive 16-byte opcodes from {@code raw} (a drain buffer). */
41:     public List<Event> decode(byte[] raw) {
42:         List<Event> events = new ArrayList<>();
43:         for (int off = 0; off + OPCODE_SIZE <= raw.length; off += OPCODE_SIZE) {
44:             if ((raw[off] & 0xFF) != CATEGORY_EVENT) {
45:                 continue;
46:             }
47:             int command = raw[off + 1] & 0xFF;
48:             int flags = u16(raw, off + 2);
49:             int a = i32(raw, off + 4);
50:             int b = i32(raw, off + 8);
51:             int c = i32(raw, off + 12);
52:             Event event = decodeOne(command, flags, a, b, c);
53:             if (event != null) {
54:                 events.add(event);
55:             }
56:         }
57:         return events;
58:     }
59: 
60:     private Event decodeOne(int command, int flags, int a, int b, int c) {
61:         return switch (command) {
62:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_DOWN -> Event.pointerDown(a, f32(b), f32(c));
63:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_UP -> Event.pointerUp(a, f32(b), f32(c));
64:             case Commands.Event.POINTER_MOVE -> Event.pointerMove(a, f32(b), f32(c), flags);
65:             case Commands.Event.KEY_DOWN -> Event.keyDown(a, b, c, flags);
66:             case Commands.Event.KEY_UP -> Event.keyUp(a, b, c);
67:             case Commands.Event.VALUE_CHANGED -> Event.valueChanged(a, f32(b));
68:             case Commands.Event.TEXT_CHANGED -> Event.textChanged(a, arenaString(b));
69:             case Commands.Event.FOCUS_CHANGED -> Event.focusChanged(a, b != 0);
70:             case Commands.Event.EDITING_CHANGED -> Event.editingChanged(a, b != 0);
71:             case Commands.Event.SUBMIT -> Event.submit(a);
72:             case Commands.Event.SCROLL -> Event.scroll(a, f32(b), f32(c));
73:             case Commands.Event.WHEEL -> Event.wheel(a, f32(b), f32(c));
74:             case Commands.Event.DATE_CHANGED -> Event.dateChanged(a, b, c);
75:             case Commands.Event.NAVIGATE -> (flags & Commands.Flags.NAVIGATE_URL) != 0
76:                     ? Event.navigate(arenaString(b))
77:                     : Event.navigateBack();
78:             default -> null;
79:         };
80:     }

82:     /** Resolve a string from the shared event arena at {@code ref} ([u32 len][bytes]). */
83:     private String arenaString(int ref) {
84:         if (ref < 0 || ringPtr == null || eventArenaOffset <= 0) {

86:         }
87:         long base = (long) eventArenaOffset + ref;
88:         if (base + 4 > ringLen) {

90:         }
91:         int len = ringPtr.getInt(base);
92:         if (len < 0 || base + 4 + len > ringLen) {
93:             return null;
94:         }
95:         byte[] bytes = ringPtr.getByteArray(base + 4, len);
96:         return new String(bytes, StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
97:     }
98: 
99:     private static int u16(byte[] raw, int off) {
100:         return (raw[off] & 0xFF) | ((raw[off + 1] & 0xFF) << 8);
101:     }
102: 
103:     private static int i32(byte[] raw, int off) {
104:         return (raw[off] & 0xFF) | ((raw[off + 1] & 0xFF) << 8)
105:                 | ((raw[off + 2] & 0xFF) << 16) | ((raw[off + 3] & 0xFF) << 24);
106:     }
107: 
108:     private static float f32(int bits) {
109:         return Float.intBitsToFloat(bits);
110:     }

1: //! # pathland-core-capi
2: //!
3: //! The minimal C ABI for the Pathland SPSC ring buffer + 16-byte opcode engine,
4: //! built as `libpathland_core` (a `cdylib`). Foreign hosts (Java FFM, Swift,
5: //! C#, …) construct the 16-byte opcodes themselves, allocate variable-length
6: //! strings into the bump arena, and push them into the shared ring **in
7: //! place** — the engine stays in Rust, the retained tree / diff stays in the
8: //! host language.
9: //!
10: //! ```c
11: //! void* h = pathland_core_create();
12: //! pathland_core_begin_frame(h);
13: //! uint8_t op[16] = { 0x01, 0x01, 0, 0, 1,0,0,0, 2,0,0,0, 0,0,0,0 };
14: //! pathland_ring_buffer_push(h, op);   // TREE::CREATE_NODE, id 1, vstack
15: //! pathland_core_end_frame(h);
16: //! // read opcodes zero-copy from pathland_core_ring_ptr(h)
17: //! pathland_core_destroy(h);
18: //! ```
19: //!
20: //! Opcode layout (little-endian): `[Category u8][Command u8][Flags u16][A u32]
21: //! [B u32][C u32]` — see `spec/OPCODE.md`.
22: 
23: use plcore::{Opcode, OPCODE_SIZE};
24: use pathland_core_transport::RingTransport;
25: 
26: /// Opaque handle to a ring host.
27: pub type CoreHandle = *mut std::ffi::c_void;
28: 
29: /// The native host: owns the shared-memory ring + arena.
30: struct CoreHost {
31:     ring: RingTransport,
32: }
33: 
34: fn as_host<'a>(handle: CoreHandle) -> &'a mut CoreHost {
35:     assert!(!handle.is_null(), "pathland_core: null handle");
36:     // SAFETY: handles come only from `pathland_core_create`.
37:     unsafe { &mut *(handle as *mut CoreHost) }
38: }
39: 
40: /// Read a 16-byte opcode from a foreign pointer.
41: fn opcode_from_ptr(opcode: *const u8) -> Option<Opcode> {
42:     if opcode.is_null() {
43:         return None;
44:     }
45:     // SAFETY: the caller guarantees `opcode` points to ≥ 16 readable bytes.
46:     let slice = unsafe { std::slice::from_raw_parts(opcode, OPCODE_SIZE) };
47:     let arr: [u8; OPCODE_SIZE] = slice.try_into().ok()?;
48:     Some(Opcode::from_bytes(&arr))
49: }

52: // Lifetime
53: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

55: /// Create a ring host over a fresh zero-copy shared ring. Returns an opaque
56: /// handle (non-null on success).
57: #[no_mangle]
58: pub extern "C" fn pathland_core_create() -> CoreHandle {
59:     let host = Box::new(CoreHost {
60:         ring: RingTransport::new(),
61:     });
62:     Box::into_raw(host) as CoreHandle
63: }
64: 
65: /// Destroy a ring host previously created by [`pathland_core_create`].
66: #[no_mangle]
67: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_destroy(handle: CoreHandle) {
68:     if !handle.is_null() {
69:         // SAFETY: `handle` is the pointer returned by `pathland_core_create`.
70:         drop(Box::from_raw(handle as *mut CoreHost));
71:     }
72: }
73: 
74: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
75: // Ring (guest → host)
76: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
77: 
78: /// Push one raw 16-byte opcode into the shared ring at `writeCursor`, advancing
79: /// it. Returns 1 on success, 0 when the ring is full or `opcode` is null.
80: #[no_mangle]
81: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_ring_buffer_push(handle: CoreHandle, opcode: *const u8) -> u8 {
82:     let Some(op) = opcode_from_ptr(opcode) else {
83:         return 0;
84:     };
85:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
86:     u8::from(guest.push_opcode(op).is_ok())
87: }
88: 
89: /// Allocate `len` bytes into the bump arena, returning the absolute arena
90: /// offset (a `u32` reference for `STYLE::SET_TEXT` / `STRING` property values).
91: /// Returns `u32::MAX` when the arena is full or `bytes` is null.
92: #[no_mangle]
93: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_arena_alloc(
94:     handle: CoreHandle,
95:     bytes: *const u8,
96:     len: u32,

111:     guest.begin_frame();
112: }

117:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
118:     guest.end_frame();
119: }

122: #[no_mangle]
123: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_frame_count(handle: CoreHandle) -> u32 {
124:     let guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
125:     guest.frame_count()
126: }

129: /// reads. Never null.
130: #[no_mangle]
131: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_ptr(handle: CoreHandle) -> *const u8 {
132:     as_host(handle).ring.buffer().as_ptr()
133: }

136: #[no_mangle]

145: /// the ring. The pointer is only valid inside this process.
146: #[no_mangle]
147: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_ring_mut(handle: CoreHandle) -> *mut RingTransport {
148:     if handle.is_null() {
149:         return std::ptr::null_mut();

155: // Events (host → guest)
156: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

158: /// Drain pending raw `EVENT`-category opcodes from the host → guest event ring,
159: /// copying each 16-byte opcode into `out`. Returns the number of events
160: /// written (≤ `max`). `out` must point to ≥ `max * 16` writable bytes.
161: #[no_mangle]
162: pub unsafe extern "C" fn pathland_core_drain_events(
163:     handle: CoreHandle,
164:     out: *mut u8,
165:     max: u32,
166: ) -> u32 {
167:     if out.is_null() || max == 0 {
168:         return 0;
169:     }
170:     let mut guest = as_host(handle).ring.producer();
171:     let events = guest.drain_event_opcodes();
172:     let n = events.len().min(max as usize);
173:     for (i, op) in events.into_iter().take(n).enumerate() {
174:         let bytes = op.to_bytes();

176:         std::ptr::copy_nonoverlapping(bytes.as_ptr(), out.add(i * 16), 16);

1: //! Shared-memory ring transport (zero-copy, SPSC).
2: //!
3: //! The producer (opcode engine) and consumer (native driver) share one linear
4: //! memory buffer containing the ring + arena. The producer writes 16-byte
5: //! opcodes via `pathland_core::Guest`; the consumer reads completed frames via
6: //! `pathland_core::Host`. No copying, no batching, no serialization — this is
7: //! the high-performance local path.
8: 
9: use pathland_core::{init_memory, Guest, Host, MemoryLayout};
10: 
11: use crate::traits::{DriverTransport, FrameSource, OpcodeBatch, TransportError};
12: 
13: /// A zero-copy SPSC shared-memory ring transport.
14: ///
15: /// Owns the linear-memory buffer (header + ring + arena). Producers and
16: /// consumers are granted short-lived `Guest`/`Host` views over the same buffer
17: /// via the borrowed methods, so opcodes flow in place with no copies.
18: #[derive(Debug)]
19: pub struct RingTransport {
20:     /// Shared linear memory (header | ring | arena).
21:     mem: Vec<u8>,
22:     /// Ring/arena geometry.
23:     layout: MemoryLayout,
24: }
25: 
26: impl RingTransport {
27:     /// Create a ring transport with a default layout and a zeroed header.
28:     pub fn new() -> Self {
29:         let layout = MemoryLayout::default();
30:         let mut mem = vec![0u8; layout.total_bytes()];
31:         init_memory(&mut mem, &layout);
32:         Self { mem, layout }
33:     }
34: 
35:     /// Create a ring transport over a caller-provided buffer/layout.
36:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
37:         Self { mem, layout }
38:     }
39: 
40:     /// The memory layout (region geometry).
41:     pub fn layout(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
42:         &self.layout
43:     }
44: 
45:     /// Create a producer view over the shared buffer (writes opcodes + arena).
46:     ///
47:     /// Drop the returned `Guest` before calling `next_frame`; producer and
48:     /// consumer must not overlap borrows.
49:     pub fn producer(&mut self) -> Guest<'_> {
50:         Guest::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout)
51:     }
52: 
53:     /// Peak at the raw underlying buffer (for embedding/custom transports).
54:     pub fn buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
55:         &self.mem
56:     }
57: }
58: 
59: impl Default for RingTransport {
60:     fn default() -> Self {
61:         Self::new()
62:     }
63: }
64: 
65: impl FrameSource for RingTransport {
66:     fn next_frame(&mut self) -> Result<Option<OpcodeBatch<'_>>, TransportError> {
67:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
68:         let mut frames = host.frames();
69:         match frames.pop() {
70:             Some(frame) => Ok(Some(OpcodeBatch::new(
71:                 frame,
72:                 crate::direction::GUEST_TO_HOST,
73:             ))),
74:             None => Ok(None),
75:         }
76:     }
77: }
78: 
79: impl DriverTransport for RingTransport {
80:     fn send_input(&mut self, event: &pathland_core::Event) -> Result<(), TransportError> {
81:         // The host writes the raw input as an EVENT-category opcode into the
82:         // host → guest event ring; the guest drains it via `drain_events`.
83:         let mut host = Host::new(&mut self.mem, &self.layout);
84:         host.send_event(event).map_err(|_| {
85:             TransportError::Protocol(crate::ProtocolError::BadInput)
86:         })
87:     }
88: }
89: 
90: impl RingTransport {
91:     /// Drain raw-input events written by the host into the host → guest event
92:     /// ring, decoding each `EVENT` opcode (guest side).
93:     pub fn drain_events(&mut self) -> Vec<pathland_core::Event> {
94:         let mut guest = self.producer();
95:         guest.drain_events()
96:     }
97: }

105:     fn ring_round_trips_frames() {

107:         // Producer writes opcodes into the shared buffer via Guest.
108:         {
109:             let mut guest = ring.producer();

111:             guest.create_node(1, 0x0010).unwrap();

153:         // Host (renderer) reports a click.
154:         DriverTransport::send_input(
155:             &mut ring,
156:             &Event::PointerUp {
157:                 target: 4,
158:                 x: 1.0,
159:                 y: 2.0,
160:                 secondary: false,
161:             },
162:         )
163:         .unwrap();
164:         // Guest (app) drains it as a typed event.
165:         assert_eq!(
166:             ring.drain_events(),
167:             vec![Event::PointerUp {
168:                 target: 4,
169:                 x: 1.0,

171:                 secondary: false,
172:             }]
173:         );
174:         assert!(ring.drain_events().is_empty());
175:     }
176: 
177:     #[test]
178:     fn next_frame_is_zero_copy() {
179:         // The ring is a single shared linear-memory buffer. Reading a frame
180:         // must borrow that buffer in place — never copy the opcode stream.
181:         // Prove two things:
182:         //  1. Reading N opcodes allocates O(1) bookkeeping, not O(N) storage
183:         //     (a copy of the opcode stream would allocate per-opcode).
184:         //  2. The arena string decoded from the frame lives inside the shared
185:         //     buffer (pointer identity), i.e. it is read in place.
186: 
187:         use std::alloc::{GlobalAlloc, Layout as AllocLayout};
188:         use std::cell::Cell;
189:         use std::thread_local;
190: 
191:         thread_local! {
192:             static COUNT: Cell<usize> = const { Cell::new(0) };
193:         }
194:         struct Counting;
195:         unsafe impl GlobalAlloc for Counting {
196:             unsafe fn alloc(&self, l: AllocLayout) -> *mut u8 {
197:                 COUNT.with(|c| c.set(c.get() + 1));
198:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
199:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.alloc(l) }
200:             }
201:             unsafe fn dealloc(&self, p: *mut u8, l: AllocLayout) {
202:                 // SAFETY: forward to the system allocator.
203:                 unsafe { std::alloc::System.dealloc(p, l) }
204:             }
205:         }
206:         #[global_allocator]
207:         static A: Counting = Counting;
208: 
209:         const OPCODES: usize = 1000;
210: 
211:         let mut ring = RingTransport::new();
212:         let buf_base = ring.buffer().as_ptr() as usize;
213:         let buf_end = buf_base + ring.buffer().len();
214: 
215:         // Producer writes opcodes + a string into the shared buffer (no copies).
216:         let arena_ref = {
217:             let mut guest = ring.producer();
218:             guest.begin_frame();
219:             for i in 0..OPCODES {
220:                 guest.create_node(i as u32 + 1, 0x0001).unwrap();
221:             }
222:             let r = guest.set_text(1, "zero-copy proof").unwrap();
223:             guest.end_frame();
224:             r
225:         };
226: 
227:         // Consumer reads the frame. Count allocations: the opcode stream is
228:         // borrowed, so allocations must be O(1), independent of the opcode count.
229:         COUNT.with(|c| c.set(0));
230:         let batch = ring.next_frame().unwrap().expect("a frame");
231:         let frame = batch.frame();
232: 
233:         let decoded: usize = frame.opcodes().count();
234:         let arena = frame.arena_str(arena_ref).expect("arena string");
235: 
236:         let allocs = COUNT.with(|c| c.get());
237: 
238:         assert_eq!(decoded, OPCODES + 1, "create_node + set_text");
239:         assert_eq!(arena, "zero-copy proof");
240: 
241:         // The arena string is read in place from the shared buffer.
242:         let str_ptr = arena.as_ptr() as usize;
243:         assert!(
244:             str_ptr >= buf_base && str_ptr < buf_end,
245:             "arena string must be borrowed from the shared ring (ptr {str_ptr:#x} outside {buf_base:#x}..{buf_end:#x})"
246:         );
247: 
248:         // No per-opcode copying: a handful of O(1) bookkeeping allocations is
249:         // fine; anything O(opcodes) would mean the opcode stream was copied.
250:         assert!(
251:             allocs < OPCODES,
252:             "reading {OPCODES} opcodes must not copy them (allocations: {allocs})"
253:         );
254:     }
255: }

14: /**
15:  * An {@link OpcodeSink} that writes opcodes zero-copy into the Rust SPSC ring via
16:  * JNA. Strings are allocated into the shared bump arena (absolute offsets). This is the
17:  * desktop/embedded path; the frame path uses {@code FrameOpcodeSink} instead.
18:  */
19: public final class RingOpcodeSink implements OpcodeSink, AutoCloseable {
20: 
21:     private final PathlandCore core;
22:     private final Pointer handle;
23: 
24:     public RingOpcodeSink() {
25:         this(PathlandCore.instance());
26:     }
27: 
28:     public RingOpcodeSink(PathlandCore core) {
29:         this.core = core;
30:         this.handle = core.create();
31:     }
32: 
33:     /** The opaque native handle (for direct ring access). */
34:     public Pointer handle() {
35:         return handle;
36:     }
37: 
38:     @Override
39:     public void beginFrame() {
40:         core.beginFrame(handle);
41:     }
42: 
43:     @Override
44:     public void endFrame() {
45:         core.endFrame(handle);
46:     }
47: 
48:     @Override
49:     public void createNode(int id, int component) {
50:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.CREATE_NODE, 0, id, component, 0);
51:     }
52: 
53:     @Override
54:     public void deleteNode(int id) {
55:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.DELETE_NODE, 0, id, 0, 0);
56:     }
57: 
58:     @Override
59:     public void insertChild(int parent, int child, int index) {
60:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.INSERT_CHILD, 0, parent, child, index);
61:     }
62: 
63:     @Override
64:     public void removeChild(int parent, int child) {
65:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.REMOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, 0);
66:     }
67: 
68:     @Override
69:     public void moveChild(int parent, int child, int newIndex) {
70:         push(Categories.TREE, Commands.Tree.MOVE_CHILD, 0, parent, child, newIndex);
71:     }
72: 
73:     @Override
74:     public void setText(int nodeId, String text) {
75:         int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, text.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
76:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_TEXT, 0, nodeId, ref, 0);
77:     }
