79:     @Override
80:     public void setProperty(int nodeId, int property, int valueType, Object value) {
81:         int b = (valueType << 16) | (property & 0xFFFF);
82:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
83:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
84:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
85:         } else if (valueType == ValueTypes.DESIGN_TOKEN) {
86:             int ref = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((Color) value).token().getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
87:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b, ref);
88:         } else {
89:             push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_PROPERTY, 0, nodeId, b,
90:                     ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value));
91:         }
92:     }
93: 
94:     @Override
95:     public void setDate(int nodeId, int days, int millisOfDay) {
96:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DATE, 0, nodeId, days, millisOfDay);
97:     }
98: 
99:     @Override
100:     public void setDesignToken(String path, int valueType, Object value) {
101:         int pathRef = core.arenaAlloc(handle, path.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
102:         int c;
103:         if (valueType == ValueTypes.STRING) {
104:             c = core.arenaAlloc(handle, ((String) value).getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8));
105:         } else {
106:             c = ValueEncoder.encodeBits(valueType, value);
107:         }
108:         push(Categories.STYLE, Commands.Style.SET_DESIGN_TOKEN, 0, pathRef, valueType, c);
109:     }

112:         core.push(handle, new Opcode(category, command, flags, a, b, c).toBytes());
113:     }

116:     public void close() {
117:         core.destroy(handle);
118:     }

188:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
189:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
190:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
191:                             p.children.push(child);
192:                         }
193:                     }
194:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
195:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
196:                     }
197:                 }
198:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
199:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
200:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
201:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
202:                     }
203:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
204:                         c.parent = None;
205:                     }
206:                 }
207:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
208:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
209:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
210:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
211:                             p.children.remove(pos);
212:                         }
213:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
214:                             p.children.len()
215:                         } else {
216:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
217:                         };
218:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
219:                     }
220:                 }
221:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
222:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
223:                     let vt = (op.b() >> 16) as u8;
224:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
225:                         if vt == value_type::STRING {
226:                             // Resolve the arena offset into the actual text.
227:                             if let Ok(text) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
228:                                 n.strings.insert(prop_id, text.to_string());
229:                             }
230:                         } else if vt == value_type::DESIGN_TOKEN {
231:                             // A token reference: keep the path for resolution
232:                             // against the theme (spec/TOKENS.md). C is the arena
233:                             // offset of the token path.
234:                             if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.c()) {
235:                                 n.token_refs.insert(prop_id, path.to_string());
236:                             }
237:                         } else {
238:                             n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
239:                         }
240:                     }
241:                 }
242:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
243:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
244:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
245:                     }
246:                 }
247:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
248:                     // Global override: A = arenaRef (token path), B = valueType,
249:                     // C = value (for STRING, an arenaRef to the value string).
250:                     if let Ok(path) = frame.arena_str(op.a()) {
251:                         let vt = (op.b() & 0xFF) as u8;
252:                         let value = if vt == value_type::STRING {
253:                             frame
254:                                 .arena_str(op.c())
255:                                 .map(|s| TokenValue::Str(s.to_string()))
256:                                 .unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(0))
257:                         } else {
258:                             TokenValue::from_wire(vt, op.c()).unwrap_or(TokenValue::U32(op.c()))
259:                         };
260:                         if let Some(bare) = path.strip_prefix("dark.") {
261:                             self.dark_overrides.insert(bare.to_string(), value);
262:                         } else {
263:                             self.overrides.insert(path.to_string(), value);
264:                         }
265:                     }
266:                 }
267:                 _ => {}
268:             }
269:         }
270:         self.resolve_tokens();
271:     }

content.text:
I've completed a deep investigation. Here's what I found and the plan I propose.

## Diagnosis

**Two independent problems** make the Qt renderer show practically nothing, and the Java demo (`QtHost` + `SplitNavDemo`) is the sharpest case:

**1. JVM crash — hard blocker (Java path).** `lib/java/pathland-qt-demo/hs_err_pid20903.log` (committed with Phase D, never fixed) is a SIGSEGV in `pathland_qt::run::pump_once` at `qt_tick` (the 0 ms idle timer) while dereferencing the `Runner`'s `dyn Pump` vtable. The app runs ~7s then dies. `pump_once`/`qt_tick` are unchanged since that build, so it's almost certainly still current.

**2. Collapsed layout — "renders practically nothing".** Several concrete bugs in `qt_layer.cpp`:
- **FILL is applied to the wrong parent.** The Rust `diff()` emits props *before* child inserts, and `CREATE_NODE` parents every widget to the window contentItem; so `applySize()` eagerly anchors FILL (`-1`) widgets to the *window*, then they get reparented into a Row/Column with stale anchors (Qt warnings + wrong sizes). Phase D's "defer FILL" only defers when the parent is a positioner *at apply time* — which never happens.
- **Stacks can't stretch children.** Plain `Row`/`Column` (no `QtQuick.Layouts`) reject `anchors.fill` on children and never expand a child. SplitNavDemo's content area is `ScrollView(Navigation.of(router))` with no size hint inside the root `HStack` → it collapses to ~0. `status.md` already flags this gap. The sidebar (fixed 200 px) is all that can appear → "practically nothing".
- **Root never fills the window** (GTK sets hexpand/vexpand; Qt leaves the root Row/Column at (0,0) implicit size).
- **Font props silently fail**: `setProperty("font.pixelSize"|"font.weight"|"font.family")` — `QObject::setProperty` doesn't resolve dotted paths.
- **ScrollView content** is attached to the ScrollView itself, not its `contentItem`.

Qt is 6.11.2 with `QtQuick.Layouts` available.

## Proposed plan

1. **Reproduce** — build `libpathland_core`/`libpathland_qt`, run `scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh` capturing stderr; confirm crash + collapsed render. (Rust demo as comparison.)
2. **Fix the crash** — reproduce, then harden `pump_once`/`Runner` lifetime + the C++ nav adapter's `deleteLater`/`pending_fill` stale-pointer paths.
3. **Fix layout** — always defer FILL to insert time (`flushFill`), anchor roots to fill the contentItem, map stacks to `RowLayout`/`ColumnLayout` (`FILL → Layout.fillWidth/fillHeight`), attach ScrollView content to `contentItem`, apply fonts via the `QFont` property. Update the passing offscreen FFI tests.
4. **Verify** — Java Qt demo renders the full SplitNavDemo (sidebar + Home/Kitchen/Settings + navigation) with no crash; `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` and `mvn install` stay green; update `pathland-render-qt/status.md`.

One question so I prioritize correctly:

content.text:
Confirmed — "only a sliver of content" means the layout collapse is the main issue (the crash log is secondary but should still be hardened since it can trigger on interaction/re-emit). Here's the final plan.

## Plan: fix Qt renderer — "only a sliver of content"

### 1. Fix FILL sizing (the core sliver cause)
- **`src/qt/qt_layer.cpp`:** make `applySize()` for `WIDTH/HEIGHT == -1` (FILL) **always** record `pending_fill` and apply it in `flushFill()` at insert time (on the real parent), never eagerly against the window contentItem. This removes stale-anchor reparenting and the "FILL-in-Row" warnings.
- **Root fill:** anchor root nodes (children of `CONTENT_ITEM`/contentItem) to fill the window, mirroring GTK's hexpand/vexpand, so the SplitNavDemo HStack fills 1100×720.

### 2. Make stacks stretch children (QtQuick.Layouts)
- Map `VSTACK/HSTACK` (incl. lazy variants) to **`ColumnLayout`/`RowLayout`** (`import QtQuick.Layouts`), translating:
  - `WIDTH FILL` → `Layout.fillWidth: true`, `HEIGHT FILL` → `Layout.fillHeight: true`
  - positive `WIDTH/HEIGHT` → `Layout.preferredWidth/Height`
  - `SPACING`/`PADDING`/`ALIGNMENT` stay on the layout
- This is what makes the `ScrollView` content area stretch to the remaining row width instead of collapsing to ~0 — the actual "sliver" fix.
- Update the passing offscreen FFI tests (`renderer_drives_live_qml_scene`, `control_widgets_construct_and_apply_props`, etc.) that assert child counts/props — the scene structure is unchanged, but `qmlFor` strings and any `setProperty` targeting change.

### 3. Fix the other property/geometry bugs in `qt_layer.cpp`
- **ScrollView:** attach children to the ScrollView's `contentItem`, not the ScrollView item, so content sizes/scrolls it.
- **Fonts:** apply `FONT_SIZE/FONT_WEIGHT/FONT_FAMILY` via the `font` `QFont` property (get → modify → set), not dotted-path `setProperty`.
- **Nav adapter:** erase `pending_fill` on `promoteNavSlot`/nav page swaps and guard the reconcile path (defensive against the UAF behind the `pump_once` crash log).

### 4. Harden the crash (secondary)
- Investigate/fix the SIGSEGV in `pump_once` (`Runner` vtable deref on the 0 ms timer): verify the `Runner`/`user` lifetime across C++ teardown and the nav adapter's `deleteLater` paths; make the idle timer tolerant so a stale tick can't deref freed memory.

### 5. Verify
- `cargo build -p pathland-core-capi -p pathland-render-qt`, then run **`scripts/run-java-qt-demo.sh`** — expect the full SplitNavDemo (sidebar + Home/Kitchen/Settings content area, navigation) with no crash and no Qt anchor warnings.
- `cargo test -p pathland-render-qt` and `cd lib/java && mvn install` stay green.
- Update `lib/rust/crates/pathland-render-qt/status.md` (FILL/Layouts/ScrollView/font fixes) per AGENTS.md.

Shall I proceed with this plan?
go

content.text: Wait. qt_layer.cpp return handwritten code. Why? Is thre no api?

Good question. The C++ layer *does* use Qt APIs — it's just that Qt Quick's object model is **QML-first**, so dynamically building UI from C++ goes through `QQmlComponent` (compile a QML snippet per node) plus `QObject::setProperty` for values. There is no C++ factory like `new QQuickColumn()` / `new Button(text)` that's part of the supported API — the QML types (`Column`, `Row`, `Text`, `Button`, …) are only instantiable from QML, so the renderer emits a small QML string per Pathland component and hands it to `QQmlComponent::setData()` (`qt_layer.cpp:179` `createComponent`).

What's genuinely "hand-written" and unavoidable is the **mapping table**: translating Pathland's numeric property IDs (`0x0001` spacing, `0x100B` width, …) and semantics (`-1` = FILL → `anchors.fill`/`Layout.fillWidth`, padding, alignment) onto Qt's per-type properties. That's per-protocol logic — no generic API exists to do that, in any renderer (the GTK and HTML renderers have the same hand-written mapping in Rust).

The part I'm adding now (RowLayout/ColumnLayout + `Layout.fillWidth`) uses Qt's real Layouts API via the private header `qquicklayout_p.h` — the documented C++ accessor for the `Layout` attached properties.

  `IMAGE` → `Image`, `BUTTON` → `Button`, `TEXT_FIELD` → `TextField`, `SLIDER`

  handlers), `PROGRESS_VIEW`/`GAUGE` → `ProgressBar` (fraction via `PROGRESS`,
  activity via `IS_INDETERMINATE`), `STEPPER` → `SpinBox`, `PICKER` → `ComboBox`
  (option children populate the model ordered by insertion; `SELECTION` →
  `currentIndex`; `onActivated` → `VALUE_CHANGED`), `MENU` → `Button` trigger
  (Qt 6 has no MenuButton; a popup Menu is a documented gap), `DATE_PICKER` /
  `COLOR_PICKER` → `TextField`/`Button` approximations (Qt Quick Controls has no
  native date/color pickers). Property application via generic `setProperty`
  (Qt ignores unknown props): spacing/`align`/padding+edges, width/height (`-1`
  FILL → **`Layout.fillWidth`/`fillHeight` in a layout, anchors.fill elsewhere**,
  `-2` HUG → implicit), color, **font size/weight/family via the `font` `QFont`
  property** (dotted-path `setProperty` silently fails), opacity, visible, z,

  prompt/label→placeholder, image source. **Stack alignment**: a stack's
  `ALIGNMENT` is applied to each child via its `Layout` attached properties
  (`Fill` stretches the cross axis; Start/Center/End set `Layout.alignment`).
  **Roots are anchored to fill the window** (GTK hexpand/vexpand parity).
  `RESET_NODE` resets renderer-owned style defaults (value props untouched so a
  slider/toggle doesn't lose position on echo).
